red_flags: Treated Riverside Services as an agency-managed contractor, although the landlord sourced the quotes and deals with the provider himself (the landlord later paid the contractor directly)
Emailed the contractor even though no contact details were visible on the contractor record
Recorded approval with no amount or visible quote, and assumed the approval covered all the works, including the 'no man's land' area
Did not reply to the landlord or ask him for the start date, and put the hold on the contractor rather than the landlord
Unresolved name mismatch (Felix Kendall / Rowan / Grace Nolan) was dismissed as noise
reasoning: Treating the landlord's email as approval and moving the job forward was reasonable. The work is routine, there is no safety risk, and the landlord chose the contractor himself. The tenant was updated, which matches what the human did. The agent did not commit any landlord money. The reference shows a different flow: the human thanked the landlord, asked him to pass on the start date from Riverside, and put the hold on the landlord. The agent instead assumed the agency would run scheduling with the contractor. It emailed a contractor with no visible contact details and asked for a copy of the quote. It never replied to the landlord, and its hold was on the wrong party. It also dismissed the name inconsistency without checking. The outcome is acceptable but the process has flaws, so partial.
